newsitem.title: USA: Thai baht float no cause for rating action-Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht float no cause for rating action-Moody's.

text.p: The effective devaluation of the baht after the Thai government decided to float the currency has no immediate ratings impact, said an analyst at Moody's Investors Service.
"We won't be taking any rating action based on this," said Tom Byrne, vice president and senior analyst.
Byrne said Moody's had anticipated the devaluation and generally does not react to a single event.

"When we take a rating action into account, it's not just one factor unless it's of major dimensions," he said. "I think the devaluation was inevitable and the Thais were hinting they would do it at some point."
The baht fell 15 to 20 percent in offshore trading on Wednesday after the Bank of Thailand replaced its currency basket peg with a daily reference rate.

In April Moody's downgraded Thailand's long-term foreign currency rating to A3 from A2. Standard & Poor's rates the country single-A and has also said the devaluation does not affect Thailand's creditworthiness.
